name: Grey roof tile (布瓦, reduction-fired, unglazed)

diffuseAlbedo.note: A first colour for Grey roof tile (布瓦, reduction-fired, unglazed): no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material.

refractiveIndex.source: Ma, Wu & Bao 2021 (Sci. Rep., PMC8526661): the blue clay brick's main mineral is quartz, with albite, mica and anorthite; Handbook of Mineralogy, 'Quartz': omega 1.544, epsilon 1.553
refractiveIndex.note: The feldspars and any glass keep the body within about 0.02 of this. The mineralogy is of a brick, not of a bu-wa tile.

porosity.source: S. Ma, Y. Wu, P. Bao, 'Experimental study on the properties of modern blue clay brick for Kaifeng People's Conference Hall', Scientific Reports 2021, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8526661/: water absorption 17.3-18.4 %, average 17.9 %; density 1.489-1.698 g/cm3, average 1.573. Corroboration: S. Sun, P. Jin, 'Characterization of decorative bricks from Qing Dynasty dwellings in southern Anhui', npj Heritage Science 13, 331 (2025), https://www.nature.com/articles/s40494-025-01902-9: water absorption about 19 %, bulk density about 1.70 g/cm3, porosity 'slightly less than 30%'
porosity.note: The source was brick, not roof tile. A thinner, harder-fired tile could be denser. Correction: the corroborating paper's page as read gives about 19 % and about 1.70 g/cm3, not the more precise 18.98-19.01 % and 1.67-1.69 quoted in the proposal.
porosity.derivation: Open porosity = water absorption x bulk density / water density = 0.179 x 1.573 = 0.2816, rounded to 0.28

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the travertine's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
